These are the materials of the three **Talking to Machines** workshops held before
the LLMSS 2026 conference at City University of Hong Kong on Tuesday 13 October
2026. Every notebook is here with its output, so you can read it in the browser
or download it and run it yourself (see [Run it yourself](setup.qmd)).

Every notebook ships with **stored model answers**, so it runs start to finish
with no network and no API key. Only the blocks where you send your own prompts
call a model.

## One method, three uses

All three workshops run the same four-step engine and point it at a different
question. Only the last step changes.

```
   stratification frame  →  synthetic subjects  →  digital interview  →  aggregation
   (who the population      (records + donors)      (repeated,             ├─ W1  MrP → public opinion
    is)                                              time-anchored)        ├─ W2  panel econometrics → market signals
                                                                           └─ W3  closed-loop search → best narrative
```

The Ohio panel built in Workshop 1 comes back as the audience in Workshop 3.

## The workshops

### Workshop 1 · AIPOP: AI polling and MrP

Build a stratification frame for Ohio, draw a silicon sample of 400 twins from
it, interview them with a large language model, and turn their answers into MrP
estimates checked against certified results and an election the twins never saw.

| Notebook | | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Building a silicon sample](W1_aipop/notebooks/01_frame_and_sample.Rmd) | The frame, the draw, and an audit against the project's own panel |
| 2 | [Personas and the digital interview](W1_aipop/notebooks/02_personas_and_interview.Rmd) | Matching census skeletons to survey donors, rendering personas, the vote interview |
| 3 | [MrP and validation](W1_aipop/notebooks/03_mrp_and_validation.Rmd) | Two MrP models, the 2026 Ohio Senate race, twelve state panels and a held-out election |

Ray Duch and Matías Fuentes Becerra ·
[source folder](https://github.com/talking-to-machines/llmss-2026-workshops/tree/main/W1_aipop)

### Workshop 2 · The Wisdom of Digital Twins

Build twins of ten financial influencers, interview them every day about the news
on a set of stocks, and turn their answers into a long–short signal, set against
the crowd and the prediction markets.

| Notebook | | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Finfluencer twins and the daily interview](W2_twins/notebooks/01_twins_and_interview.Rmd) | Profile cards, the interview prompt, and what a twin says about a stock |
| 2 | [From twin answers to a market signal](W2_twins/notebooks/02_signals_and_backtest.Rmd) | Panel regressions, a backtest, and a replay of a ten-agent deliberation |

Ray Duch and Matías Fuentes Becerra ·
[source folder](https://github.com/talking-to-machines/llmss-2026-workshops/tree/main/W2_twins)

### Workshop 3 · The Silicon Audience

Write a message, watch a twin panel score it, and improve it. Once for a political
ad, once for a closing argument before the Supreme Court.

| Block | | |
|---|---|---|
| Silicon Voters | [Ads for five kinds of voter](W3_audience/notebooks/02_silicon_voters.Rmd) | A model writes ads for Ohio voters; you improve its prompt in three stages, scored by the twins and by model judges |
| Silicon Jury | [A justice twin, one case, by hand](W3_legal/notebooks/01_justice_twins.Rmd) | Run one justice twin on one case, compare it with the full bench and the Court, change one input |

Ray Duch and Laurenz Günther, with Matías Fuentes Becerra ·
source folders: [Silicon Voters](https://github.com/talking-to-machines/llmss-2026-workshops/tree/main/W3_audience),
[Silicon Jury](https://github.com/talking-to-machines/llmss-2026-workshops/tree/main/W3_legal)

## Data

The notebooks use public data (the ACS 2019–2023 five-year PUMS, the
Cooperative Election Study 2020–2025, and certified election results) and
aggregate results (district, county and cell totals, never an individual) from
the Talking to Machines digital-twin panels. The personas are built on synthetic
skeletons from the census, not on voter-file records. Each workshop folder has a
`data/README.md` with the source of every file.

Only the Ohio panel files are public. The other states' panel results, used in
Workshop 1, Notebook 3, Section 7, carry non-commercial terms. This site shows
their output, but the files are not in the repository.

## The method

- **Talking to Machines**: an international collaboration of academics and
  industry researchers, directed by Sonja Vogt (HEC Lausanne) and Ray Duch
  (Nuffield College, Oxford), funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation.
  The frames, panels and vote module in these notebooks come from its
  digital-twin work.
- **PoSSUM**: Cerina and Duch, *Protocol for Surveying Social Media Users with
  Multimodal LLMs*.
